- R049 = OIML recommendation R49 (water meters? Actually R49 is water meters for cold potable water)
- 2006 = the year of the OIML R49-1:2006 edition
- NL1 = issuing authority code (NMi Certin B.V., Netherlands)
- 2012.01 = certificate number issued in 2012, number 01
- Rev. 3 = revision 3

Document form: R49-1/2006-NL1-12.01 revision 3
- R49-1 = recommendation R49-1 (part 1 of R49, metrological requirements)
- 2006 = edition year
- NL1 = authority
- 12.01 = certificate number 12.01 (shortened form of 2012.01)
- revision 3

Also the context header comments confirm: cert_id: 3521, num: R049/2006-NL1-2012.01 Rev. 3 — the register value matches the document's embedded metadata.

The PDF filename: r049-2006-nl1-2012-01-rev3.pdf confirms 2012.01.

So both forms denote the same certificate: R49-1 vs R049 — R49-1 is part 1 of R 49; "R049" with zero-padding is the same. 2012.01 vs 12.01 — year format abbreviation (2012 → 12). "Rev. 3" vs "revision 3" — same.

The rule: "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form."

So verdict: same-entity, best_value = register's canonical form "R049/2006-NL1-2012.01 Rev. 3".

One short sentence why: Both forms denote the same R49-1:2006 certificate issued by NL1 — "R49-1" vs "R049" is zero-padding/format drift and "12.01" abbreviates year "2012.01", plus the certificate's own embedded metadata (cert_id 3521, num matching register) confirms identity; use the register's canonical form.
